A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PDFBench and retain identifiable tasks, metrics, analyses, and results. All 26 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–10 and empirical analyses of metric relationships in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations, an overlap analysis in Table 5, and a mutation experiment in Figure 5, alongside retained metric analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed Repeat computation in Algorithm 1 is identical after normalizing whitespace. Neither version introduces a protein-generation model; the newly included generators are cited baselines.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates keyword guidance on 642 CAMEOTest proteins from 2020–2023. V2 replaces this with SwissTest, containing 1,057 SwissProt proteins released during January–August 2025, and evaluates GO-only, IPR-only, and combined guidance. The description test set is retained under the name MolinstTest.

E2.justification: V2 adds ProDVa to description and keyword comparisons, ProteoGAN to GO guidance, and CFP-Gen to the keyword settings. It removes the separately evaluated fine-tuned ProteinDT and PAAG variants. ProDVa also replaces fine-tuned ProteinDT in the structural-alignment and retrieval-strategy analyses.

E3.justification: V2 uses official weights without additional fine-tuning, replacing v1's mixed original/fine-tuned evaluation policy. It adds RITA perplexity, GO recovery, structural novelty/diversity, and maximum-similarity Hard novelty variants. The stated retrieval-negative pool changes from training data in v1 Appendix B.3 to test data in v2 Appendix C.2; this establishes a reported protocol revision, not necessarily a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds threshold-based overlap analyses for three models in Appendix B.3 and mutation-sensitivity tests on 1,000 natural proteins, separating motif, non-motif, and overall mutations. V1's fine-tuning comparisons disappear. The PPL/foldability and repetition analyses are retained, while selected models change in the alignment and retrieval analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report averaging over three runs with different random seeds. V2 retains uncertainty values in the description-result appendices but removes them throughout the keyword-result tables, where v1 reported them extensively. This substantially reduces uncertainty reporting without establishing fewer runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results for new models, SwissTest settings, metrics, overlap checks, and mutations, while removing fine-tuned-model results. Matched description results also change: Pinal's Rep-5 is 58.13 in v1 Table 3 and 4.73 in v2 Table 6. Keyword results concern a replaced test set, so their differences do not establish same-setting gains. V2 Tables 3 and 10 also disagree on alignment-column labels.

T1.justification: V2 extends the mathematical metric definitions with Hard novelty based on maximum similarity, structural novelty/diversity, and GO recovery, and explicitly handles empty annotation sets. Keyword inputs are redefined from named positional intervals to GO/IPR terms. These are localized definition changes; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from five models and 22 metrics to eight models and 16 metrics. More substantively, the contributions shift from large training-dataset collection toward SwissTest, expanded keyword settings, and explicit claims of contamination-controlled evaluation fairness. The overarching unified-benchmark and metric-correlation contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about IPR versus GO constraints, combined guidance, and ProTrek's sensitivity to local motifs, alongside new assurances about evaluation fairness. It removes the fine-tuning-benefit discussion. The limitations change from unequal access to baseline training code in v1 to the limited SwissTest sample size in v2.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands benchmark documentation through the SwissTest construction query, explicit dataset counts, keyword-to-text templates, supported-keyword counts, and filtering/GO-ancestor substitution instructions. It also adds a reproducibility statement asserting code and dataset availability. The project-page link remains unchanged; actual external availability is not established by this comparison.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for ProDVa, ProteoGAN, CFP-Gen, GO, DeepGO-SE, and Foldseek, and removes dataset-specific references such as CAMEO. The central positioning against fragmented prior evaluations remains. Much of the existing related-work material is retained and relocated.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark exposition, and results discussions undergo extensive rewriting. Tasks and datasets are combined, metrics are reorganized into six dimensions, and baseline and related-work descriptions are redistributed between the main text and appendices. The checklist is removed, and author/header text changes.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the benchmark overview and task diagrams, adds baseline-support, prompt-template, overlap, and mutation displays, and removes the old dataset-distribution figure. Main and appendix result tables are extensively regrouped, including a new main-text keyword comparison. Typography, headers, and figure placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful task coverage, structural metrics, overlap and mutation checks, and curation documentation. These gains coexist with lost keyword uncertainty reporting and consequential inconsistencies: Tables 3 and 10 assign different meanings to alignment columns, and the introduction swaps the PPL correlations shown in Figure 3. V1 already had inconsistent retrieval values between Tables 2 and 5. The substantial additions and unresolved reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
